body:
A supported `LANCE_DEFAULT_IO_BUFFER_SIZE=8388608` setting makes this clamp panic: its minimum is 16 MiB while `DEFAULT_IO_BUFFER_SIZE` supplies an 8 MiB maximum. Both indexed and plan execution paths construct this budget, so existing processes using smaller scan buffers cannot perform merges after this change. The default is cached, so changing the environment after initialization also requires restarting the process.

Apply the floor before taking the configured ceiling, or cap the floor by that ceiling, and cover a buffer below 16 MiB in a regression test.

Reproduced on `491326fb1d6d5aa71e6838ad888d4f9629405d14`:

```sh
LANCE_DEFAULT_IO_BUFFER_SIZE=8388608 cargo test -p lance --test merge_insert_memory_bound -- --nocapture
```

Expected: the merge succeeds under its 48 MiB pool. Observed: `min > max. min = 16777216, max = 8388608` at this line. The same test passes with the override unset.

Fixed in 5b40637a1: the floor now applies before the configured ceiling, so `scan_io_bytes` is `max(pool / 4, 16 MiB)` capped by `DEFAULT_IO_BUFFER_SIZE`, never above it. Both paths share `MergeBudget::new`. `test_scan_io_bytes` covers an 8 MiB configured buffer, and your reproducer passes with `LANCE_DEFAULT_IO_BUFFER_SIZE=8388608`. Also rebased over #10062; the lineage-spill provider now runs under the merge budget's session.

Fixed in [5b40637a1](https://github.com/lance-format/lance/commit/5b40637a1a16cfef153a22b1bcab768fe172b439): the shared merge budget applies the 16 MiB floor before the configured ceiling. I verified that an 8 MiB ceiling yields an 8 MiB budget without panicking, and that the normal floor and ceiling cases retain their intended values.

suggestion: instead of creating a new test binary, could we fold this into: https://github.com/lance-format/lance/tree/main/rust/lance/tests/resource_test

diff_hunk:
@@ -1129,6 +1127,92 @@ fn one_shot_provider(stream: SendableRecordBatchStream) -> Result<Arc<dyn TableP
     Ok(Arc::new(StreamingTable::try_new(schema, vec![partition])?))
 }
 
+/// One merge's memory budget: the session it plans and executes under, and
+/// the target scan's share of that session's pool.
+///
+/// The session carries Lance's configured pool (`LANCE_MEM_POOL_SIZE`) so an
+/// oversized hash-join build fails with `ResourcesExhausted` instead of
+/// growing. Join reordering is off: the merge joins put the source on the
+/// build side, and DataFusion's statistics-driven swap would otherwise move a
+/// target with few (but wide) rows back onto it. Repartitioning is off too:
+/// the join collects the source once and streams the target through it in
+/// one partition, so no `RepartitionExec` coalesces target batches up to the
+/// session batch size outside the pool, and unmatched source rows come out
+/// in source order. The scan still decodes in parallel; only the probe is
+/// single-threaded.
body: issue(blocking): this disables a lot of optimizations that seem like they should be good, at least in some situations. Making the join single threaded seems like it would make things slower, especially for large inputs. Could you run our benchmark suites before and after this change and post the comparison in this PR?

body: Is there a way we could have the memory limiter be aware of partitioning and allow a certain amount of parallelism as long as we had enough memory?
